name: What's the difference between steady-state cardio and HIIT for functional fitness goals?
description: Steady-state builds aerobic endurance, while HIIT improves both aerobic and anaerobic capacity. Cave Training uses both for well-rounded fitness.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between steady-state cardio and HIIT for functional fitness goals?

acceptedAnswer.text: Steady-state cardio involves maintaining a consistent, moderate intensity for an extended period, improving aerobic endurance. HIIT (High-Intensity Interval Training) alternates short bursts of intense exercise with brief recovery periods, enhancing both aerobic and anaerobic capacity. At Cave Training, we often incorporate both to develop a well-rounded functional fitness base, and the choice depends on your specific goals and time availability.
